classification.difficultyReason: Combine exact surd perimeter and area calculations with Pythagoras to obtain each diagonal.

content.prompt: For each rectangle, find (in exact form) the perimeter and area, and the length of the diagonal.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle; four right-angle markers; bottom side sqrt(3), right side sqrt(2); no diagonal supplied. Ordinary source blue outline rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent sides sqrt(3) and sqrt(2), all angles right.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; diagonal and calculated answers remain hidden.

answer.short: Perimeter: $2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{3}$ units. Area: $\sqrt{6}$ square units. Diagonal: $\sqrt{5}$ units.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P&=2(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2})\\P&=2\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}\text{ units}\\A&=\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{2}\\A&=\sqrt{6}\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
By Pythagoras' theorem,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=(\sqrt{3})^2+(\sqrt{2})^2\\d^2&=3+2\\d&=\sqrt{5}\text{ units}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle; four right-angle markers; bottom side sqrt(5), right side sqrt(3); no diagonal supplied. Ordinary source blue outline rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent sides sqrt(5) and sqrt(3), all angles right.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; diagonal and calculated answers remain hidden.

answer.short: Perimeter: $2\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{5}$ units. Area: $\sqrt{15}$ square units. Diagonal: $2\sqrt{2}$ units.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P&=2(\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{3})\\P&=2\sqrt{5}+2\sqrt{3}\text{ units}\\A&=\sqrt{5}\times\sqrt{3}\\A&=\sqrt{15}\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$
By Pythagoras' theorem,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=(\sqrt{5})^2+(\sqrt{3})^2\\d^2&=5+3\\d&=\sqrt{8}\\d&=2\sqrt{2}\text{ units}.\end{align*}$$
